note: Linux, libx264/libx265 through PyAV, 480 pictures per stream (adversarial: 600); NOT PS5 streams, not the PS5's encoder. Each stream goes through PushStreamDedup and ContentDedup as in the engine. droppedNew: a new game picture the engine would drop (the number that matters). droppedNewIdentical: of those, pictures whose decoded luma is the same as the picture before in every sample (nothing visible lost). falseRepeat: a new picture the classifier called a repeat. missedRepeat: a repeat that is kept (harmless). worstDroppedPixel: the largest luma sample difference of any dropped new picture. Block differences: 16x16 block means against the previous decoded picture, 8-bit code values. Classifier: include/veyra/remoteplay/StreamCadence.h defaults.
thresholds: StreamCadenceConfig defaults as frozen in commit 114239e0 (before the hold-out set was scored with them): ratio 0.4, identical 0.6, ceiling 2.5, meanVeto 4, meanRatio 0.25, meanFloor 1, shareVeto 0.9, cutFactor 3, marginGain 2, confidenceFloor 0.5, rhythmFloor 1.2, pixelCeiling 16, pixelRatio 0.4, lockSteps 6, fastLockSteps 3, unlockMisses 2; pixel step 4 (kStreamChangePixelStep). No 'identical' shortcut; a picture number only inside a locked rhythm with confidence at or above the floor.
holdoutNote: The hold-out streams (same content and encoder settings as before the review) were made again with the new measurement, without printing a statistic, and scored once with the thresholds frozen in 114239e0. The same hold-out content had been scored once before, with the first classifier (commit 0779a3a6); that result did not drive the changes (the reviewer's scenes and the tune and adversarial sets did), but it is the second look at this content.
